transcript.text: Shark NV602UK has lost loads of suction and whistles. Found a split in the flexible hose near the handle end. Is it the hose I need?

Weak suction is usually an airflow issue. Please switch off and unplug the vacuum (or remove the battery) before starting. Empty the bin or replace the bag, then wash the filters in cold water only. It is vital that a washed filter is completely dry for at least 24 hours before reinserting it, as dampness chokes airflow. You can refer to the image shown above for guidance. Was the bin full or a filter clogged (and is it sorted), is a filter damaged, or was it all clean already?
[Helpful to see: image "Poor suction — what to check first" — Lost suction is usually a full bin, a dirty filter or a blockage in the hose, tube or floor head — check and clear those before suspecting the motor. Switch off and unplug first. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
Did the filters and bin already last week, little change. Hose is clear, and when I cover the split with my hand the suction is much better. So is it just the hose I need to replace?

Thanks for confirming that the bin and filters are clean and there are no blockages, yet suction remains weak. Please switch off and unplug the vacuum first to ensure safety. Then turn the floorhead over and cut away any hair or thread wrapped around the brush bar, checking that it turns freely by hand. Was it tangled (and is it clear now), is the brush bar broken, or was it already clean?
The brushroll spins fine and the suction is only bad because of the split, covering it fixes it. So is it just the hose, or the hose and handle together? Not sure which to buy.

[Heading: Internal seal or the motor area]
With the bin, filters, hose and brush bar all clear but the suction still weak, the problem is inside — usually a leaking seal or the motor area. That needs a repairer to look at — I'm not recommending a motor or any part from weak suction alone.
